justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: Consultation Management Component and Video Media Server handle R-01; E-Prescription Routing Component handles R-02; AI Symptom Checker Container with Clinical Rules Engine covers R-03; Consent Enforcement Component fulfills R-04.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Low-bandwidth streaming is optimized by the ABR Controller, database throughput is maintained by PgBouncer, and high-volume audit logs are streamed asynchronously using the BigQuery Log Ingestion Service and Redis rate limiting.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability is addressed via HL7 FHIR and mTLS connections to US Pharmacy Systems, EU National E-Prescription Gateways, and National Health Registries, alongside OAuth 2.0/OIDC federated identity with External Identity Providers.
justifications.usability: Both Patients and Clinicians are served through tailored interfaces via React Web Application and React Native Mobile App, supported by API Client & Localization Layer and dedicated low-bandwidth WebRTC UI components.
justifications.reliability: Degraded network operation is mitigated by ABR Controller and State & Offline Sync Engine (WatermelonDB). However, explicit automated cross-region failover and disaster recovery patterns between europe-west3 and us-central1 are not fully detailed.
justifications.security: Strict controls are enforced using Regional Schema Partition Manager with RLS, JWT/Auth Validation Filter, mTLS via Anthos Service Mesh, Cloud KMS envelope encryption, and audit immutability in BigQuery for HIPAA and GDPR compliance.
justifications.maintainability: The architecture is modular, separating domains into Core Services Container, AI Symptom Checker Container, and Video Media Server with clean internal component boundaries (e.g., Model Orchestrator, Traceability Logger).
justifications.portability: Target GCP regions (europe-west3, us-central1) are supported with containerized workloads (Cloud Run/GKE). However, architectural components depend tightly on proprietary GCP managed services like BigQuery and Cloud Endpoints, limiting multi-cloud portability.

PERF-01.justification: LiveKit SFU with ABR and dedicated signaling handles high concurrency, but dynamic horizontal autoscaling mechanisms for peak SFU media clusters are not explicitly defined.
elements: GCP Cloud Endpoints / Envoy API Gateway
sensitivity_points: SFU bandwidth and media stream distribution under sudden concurrent session spikes
tradeoffs: SFU media proxying ensures lower client bandwidth but increases server CPU overhead

PERF-02.justification: FastAPI combined with async audit logging to BigQuery and in-memory rule processing comfortably supports ~14 requests per second well within the 3-second SLA.
sensitivity_points: Inference latency and asynchronous emission of audit records to BigQuery
tradeoffs: Asynchronous audit logging optimizes API latency but risks audit queue lag during spikes

AVAIL-01.justification: The dedicated LiveKit ABR Controller dynamically drops media quality below 300 kbit/s, while client-side offline sync engines safeguard clinical notes against disconnections.
sensitivity_points: Real-time bandwidth estimation thresholds for degrading video before session disconnect
tradeoffs: Degrading to low-framerate video preserves connectivity at the expense of visual clarity

AVAIL-02.justification: The architecture only targets a single US region (us-central1); complete failure of that region leaves no secondary US failover location, violating data residency constraints.
elements: GCP Cloud Endpoints / Envoy API Gateway
sensitivity_points: Absence of a secondary in-country cloud region for US data disaster recovery
tradeoffs: Single-region deployment simplifies data residency but eliminates regional fault tolerance

MOD-01.justification: The E-Prescription Routing Component manages compliance and routing, but does not specify a pluggable adapter architecture to isolate diverse national EU standards into separate modules.
sensitivity_points: Modularity and decoupling of national e-prescription protocol handlers
tradeoffs: Monolithic routing component reduces deployment overhead but increases regression risks across country updates

MOD-02.justification: Immutable, version-tagged model weights with SHA-256 validation in Cloud Storage and structured BigQuery traceability logging enable instant rollbacks and complete audit traceability.
sensitivity_points: Strict coupling between active model weight versions and emitted BigQuery log records
tradeoffs: Strict model artifact validation slows deployment startup but guarantees regulatory traceability

SEC-01.justification: Consent Enforcement Component and PostgreSQL Row-Level Security strictly enforce cross-region boundaries, rejecting unconsented requests and producing immutable audit logs in BigQuery.
sensitivity_points: Correct propagation of consent claims across API gateway tokens to database RLS policies
tradeoffs: Enforcing RLS and consent validation on every query adds marginal processing latency

SEC-02.justification: Consent updates in Cloud SQL immediately take effect for online queries via the Consent Enforcement Component, though mechanisms for retracting already-streamed BigQuery analytics data are unstated.
sensitivity_points: Synchronization between transactional consent states and downstream research data pipelines
tradeoffs: Synchronous consent verification prevents unauthorized sharing but requires frequent database lookups
